data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'akhlaq', meaning 'moral conduct' or 'good behavior'. In Islamic and Sufi traditions, ekhlaq refers to the cultivation of moral and ethical virtues through spiritual practices and self-discipline. The name Ekhlaq carries the meaning “Moral conduct, good behavior” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ekhlaq usually hope their child will grow to embody moral conduct, good behavior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: Ekhlaq holds great spiritual significance, especially within Sufi circles, as it is considered a means to achieving a closer relationship with Allah. It involves self-reflection, self-discipline, and spiritual practices aimed at cultivating moral virtues and good character. By focusing on ekhlaq, individuals are encouraged to live a virtuous life that reflects the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the moral values of the Islamic faith. Ultimately, the goal of ekhlaq is to purify the soul and strengthen one's connection with Allah, leading to a more fulfilling and meaningful life.
